A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flexora and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite extensive rewriting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original accuracy, runtime, layer-selection, ablation and qualitative evaluation results for Flexora.

after.justification: Original empirical results are retained and expanded with additional ablations, adaptation experiments and numerical smoothness analysis in Section 5 and Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: The core relaxation, alternating optimization, positive-alpha layer selection and retraining procedure is retained. Appendices C.3 and C.5 add adaptations using MoSLoRA/LoReFT and backbone parameters for full-parameter tuning. These are limited extensions of the existing framework; separating initialization into its own stage is primarily explanatory.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, RACE-mid/high, BoolQ, ARC-e/c and OBQA, including the appendix comparison with LoRAShear. The added instruction-model, rank and tuning experiments reuse existing tasks and change model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated LoRA-SP and LoRA-FA baselines and removes LLaMA Pro, QLoRA, OLoRA, LoRA+, GaLore, PiSSA and ROSA. The adaptation comparison also adds LoReFT and MoSLoRA alongside the retained DoRA and rsLoRA comparisons (v1 Table 8; v3 Table 10).

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled rank and K/T sweeps, full-parameter and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct configurations, and smoothness measurements using parameter perturbations and ten sampled inputs. The existing search-sample sweep is also revised from common 1,000–20,000-sample budgets to dataset-specific budgets including 1,267 and 4,887 samples (v1 Table 10; v3 Table 14). These establish changes to reported protocols without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds an ablation removing final fine-tuning (Table 3), rank and K/T sensitivity studies (Tables 1, 15 and 16), and smoothness and learned-alpha analyses (Figures 14–15). Original random-layer ablations and loss analyses remain. Five qualitative examples are removed when v1 Appendix C.7 becomes v3 Appendix G.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and retain the same three random-layer configurations and their average, without training-seed replication, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3's ten-input smoothness average specifies evaluation sampling rather than repeated-training uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds numerous results, including average accuracy of 63.80 without final fine-tuning versus 86.46 with it (Table 3), and a MoSLoRA combination that decreases the reported average from 86.73 to 86.54 (Table 10). Existing entries also change: Llama3-8B LoRA's PIQA accuracy changes from 73.72 to 76.39 in the cross-model table, and 1,000-sample Winogrande accuracy changes from 76.40 to 83.04 in the search study. The main rank-8 Flexora scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives a linear-network smoothness bound accounting separately for frozen backbone weights and trainable adapter components, culminating in Equation 23. This substantially extends v1's depth-based MLP argument and adds a finite-difference estimation formulation. The original propositions and Appendix A proofs are largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the central claims that automatic HPO/UD layer selection mitigates LoRA overfitting, reduces fine-tuning resources and improves downstream performance. Added supporting experiments and the three-stage exposition do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: V3 replaces the explanation that adapter selection makes the network shallower with an adapter-dependent smoothness argument. It adds interpretations concerning local optima, full-parameter overfitting and MoSLoRA incompatibility. The new Limitations section expands the existing small-validation-set warning with a hyperparameter-separation explanation and explicitly qualifies compatibility with other adaptation methods.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents train/validation/test counts (Table 5), fine-tuning epochs (Table 6), the BoolQ 80/20 training-validation partition, detailed search times and the numerical perturbation procedure. These supplement already extensive configuration information; most existing hyperparameters, prompt templates, hardware and framework disclosures remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations and discussion for MoSLoRA, LoReFT, VeRA, rsLoRA, AFLoRA and LLM-adapters, while removing several model-report citations. Its central positioning as automated layer-level selection compared with manually designed parameter-level approaches remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are substantially rewritten, with initialization receiving its own subsection. Appendices are reorganized from A–C into A–G, separating losses and qualitative cases. The conclusion is shortened, future-work discussion is removed, and Limitations and Ethics Statement sections are added.

P2.justification: V3 restructures Table 1 with rank groupings, relocates the main-text timing table to Appendix C, and adds several tables and Figures 14–15. It also redraws Figure 4, reformats the cross-model table and example boxes, and changes typography and page layout throughout. Most original loss plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The new stage, rank and K/T ablations provide more direct evidence about design choices, while split/epoch disclosures and explicit compatibility limitations improve transparency. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Figure 3 retains baseline values revised in Table 9, and Appendix C.1 uses a 0.08-hour search cost although Table 14 associates the headline HellaSwag accuracy with a 0.8-hour search.
